title: Capacity slicing tradeoffs: hosted / dedicated / private proposal
content:
Summary:

This note proposes a capacity-slicing approach for customer POCs that need predictable latency and cost while allowing periodic bursts and private data isolation. The goal is a single POC blueprint that a solutions engineer can tailor quickly to hosted, dedicated, and private options without reworking major engineering work. Focus areas: routing policy, slice sizing, burst fallback, cost math, security constraints, observability and an experiment plan.

Context / background:
- Customer: mid-size retail analytics platform evaluating an assistant for agent support + embedding search. Expected steady-state traffic: 300 QPS at 2k tokens per request during U.S. business hours (8–20 local). Peak bursts (promotions): up to 1,200 QPS for short windows (5–30 minutes) driven by campaigns.
- Constraint: PII in prompts/embeddings requires optional customer-managed KMS and audit logs on private mode.
- Timebox: 6-week POC with two staged rollouts (internal demo -> live limited customer).

Problem statement:
- Hosted alone is cheapest to start but customers worry about data residency and predictable tail latency during bursts.
- Dedicated gives isolation and predictable throughput but has higher baseline cost and longer provisioning lead time.
- Private (VPC/on-prem) solves compliance but increases ops surface and lengthens time-to-value.

Proposed approach (capacity slicing):
- Define three logical slices for the POC across deployment modes:
  1) baseline slice: covers steady-state 300 QPS (90% traffic tail target)
  2) reserved burst slice: short-term capacity reserved on Dedicated (or reserved hosted burst pool) sized for 600 QPS extra for prioritized traffic
  3) elastic fallback slice: overflow routed to lower-cost model variant (smaller model / more quantized) running in hosted with aggressive batching, applied only to non-critical routes (e.g., background embeddings refresh)

How the slices map to deployment modes:
- Hosted-first POC: baseline on hosted managed fleet (fastest), reserved burst via pooled hosted burst capacity with SLO tradeoffs, elastic fallback to more-quantized hosted variant.
- Dedicated-preview POC: baseline pinned to a dedicated GPU pool (guaranteed latency), reserved burst via short-term burst instances in the same dedicated pool or cross-region fallback, elastic fallback to hosted variant for non-sensitive requests.
- Private-hardened POC: baseline on customer VPC nodes (private control plane), reserved burst brokered through Dedicated (for capacity) or a secure interconnect to hosted burst pool depending on network policy, elastic fallback limited or disabled if data residency prohibits external routing.

Routing & policy rules (draft):
- Route type: priority-tagged per-request (critical / interactive / batch).
- Critical interactive: prefer baseline slice; on baseline saturation, failover to reserved burst slice in same trust domain. If still saturated and customer allows, fall back to elastic variant (reduced quality) after circuit-breaker delay (200ms).
- Batch / async: route to elastic fallback immediately when baseline >60% to preserve interactivity.
- Quotas & circuit breakers: per-tenant RPS ceilings, soft throttles with 429 + retry-after, hard-cut with 503 for sustained overload.

Back-of-envelope capacity numbers (example POC sizing):
- Baseline (300 QPS): assume avg 2k tokens / request, 32 token/sec generation on chosen model => GPU concurrency ~ 12 requests per A100-like GPU (guestimate). Baseline: 25 GPUs to meet latency 95th < 250ms.
- Reserved burst (600 QPS): additional 50% of baseline GPUs (12 GPUs) kept warm or thin instances able to spin up in < 90s (warm pool).
- Elastic fallback variant: quantized 4-bit variant with ~3–4x throughput improvement; can be hosted multi-tenant with autoscaling.
- Cost model sketch (monthly): baseline dedicated GPUs ~$XXk/month per 10-GPU block; hosted consumption model costs ~Y/token. Provide both and simulate 30% of traffic hitting fallback during promotions to compare total. (Numbers to populate per-customer pricing)

Security / compliance notes:
- Private mode: require KMS integration (customer-managed), VPC peering or PrivateLink, and audit log retention policy >= 1 year. Ensure embeddings never leave VPC unless customer signs off.
- Dedicated: apply tenant network isolation and per-tenant key ring; restrict admin plane access to SSO groups.
- Hosted: ensure encrypted transit and at-rest; document retention window and deletion policy for PII-heavy workloads.

Observability and SLOs:
- Per-slice telemetry: token/sec, p90/p99 latency per route tag, model fallback frequency, tail-kv-cache hit rates. Dashboards: baseline, burst, fallback.
- Alerts: fallback rate > 5% sustained for 5m, p99 latency > 1s, burst pool spin-up failures.
- Tracing: attach request path with slice tag to traces for root-cause.

POC experiment plan (6 weeks):
- Week 0 (prep): confirm security questionnaire answers; provision baseline hosted or dedicated depending on customer preference. Jira: JIRA-PLT-1120 assign infra tasks.
- Week 1: deploy baseline model and basic dashboards; sanity tests with synthetic load.
- Week 2: add reserved burst pool and implement routing policy; smoke test spike scenarios (1–5m, 1k QPS).
- Week 3: deploy elastic fallback variant and tune batching/quantization; run quality regression tests against baseline prompts.
- Week 4: run controlled promotion simulation with 3x traffic for 10 minutes; measure quality delta and cost.
- Week 5: harden security (KMS, logs), collect feedback and iterate.
- Week 6: demo + handoff + runbook and next-step pricing proposal.

Success criteria (example):
- Latency: p95 interactive <= 300ms during steady-state, p95 <= 600ms during burst for prioritized routes.
- Availability: < 1% request error rate during spikes.
- Quality: fallback variant should keep ROUGE/semantic-similarity >= 0.90 vs baseline on core prompt set.
- Cost: combined cost of baseline + burst should be <= customer target TCO (to be filled).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: burst cold-starts cause unacceptable tail latency. Mitigation: warm pooled instances and fast spin-up scripts + pre-warming during scheduled campaigns.
- Risk: data residency prevents using hosted fallback. Mitigation: provide dedicated bursting or disable fallback; document cost impact.
- Risk: model quality regressions when using quantized fallback. Mitigation: run eval set and guardrails; auto-roll back fallback if regression > threshold.

Open questions for customer / next meeting:
- Are short lived bursts allowed to route outside customer VPC under any conditions? (Yes / No)
- What is the committed monthly baseline spending target? This defines dedicated sizing.
- Desired audit log retention period and KMS responsibilities.

Action items (owners):
- Priya: finalize cost sketch and prepare two price scenarios (hosted-first vs dedicated commit) by next Tue.
- Evan: prototype routing policy and flagging in the gateway; PR -> github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/802.
- Lucas: prepare evaluation prompt set and regression harness; link results to Confluence (CONFLUENCE-POC-4821).

Appendix: quick checklist for SEs when using this blueprint:
- Confirm data sensitivity level and KMS needs.
- Choose baseline: hosted if <6 weeks to demo and customer ok with hosted; dedicated if they require predictable tails and commit.
- Define three slices and map which routes fall into each bucket.
- Pre-size warm pool for bursts; validate spin-up time under load.
- Run quality checks on quantized fallback and set rollback thresholds.

Notes / rough thoughts (working):
- Consider offering a managed "burst buffer" add-on for customers who want private baseline but occasional burst capacity without provisioning extra dedicated hardware.
- Might be useful to build a small cost calculator snippet (sheet) that takes steady QPS, burst length/frequency and shows hosted vs dedicated vs hybrid cost curves.

End of note.
